section_summary.extract_value: This section describes a sample of 840 students (438 boys, 402 girls) from three Brazilian cities in São Paulo State aged 13–17, with gender-specific mean ages (boys 15.50, girls 15.51) and mean BMIs (boys 21.87, girls 21.67). It also reports a second independent test-retest sample of 46 students (19 boys, 27 girls; Mage = 14.02, MBMI = 20.32) who completed the BAS-2 twice within two weeks to assess temporal stability.
section_summary.evidence_source: Participant ages ranged from 13 to 17 years, with a mean age of 15.50 (SD=1.20) for boys and 15.51 (SD=1.18) for girls. Their self-reported BMI ranged from 13.55 to 43.98 kg/m2, being their mean BMI of 21.87 (SD=3.52) for boys and 21.67 (SD=3.71) for girls. To analyse BAS-2's temporal stability, a second independent sample of students comprising 19 boys and 27 girls (Mage = 14.02, SDage = 0.93, MBMI = 20.32, SDBMI= 3.03) completed the instrument twice within a two-week period.
